proof_skeleton_nl: First rewrite the original summand by the standalone identity ((q^d;q^d)_k)^2/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k/(-q^d;q^d)_k, so the theorem difference becomes the specialization a=1 of a normalized auxiliary sum S_{d,r,n}(a,q). After multiplying by the common denominator D_{d,n}(q), the cleared difference is F_{d,r,n}(a,q). The only hard input is the bottleneck creative-microscoping lemma asserting that F_{d,r,n}(a,q) is divisible by [n]_q(a-q^{rn})(1-a q^{rn}). This replaces the rejected false special-value branch entirely. Specializing a=1 gives divisibility by [n]_q(1-q^{rn})^2; the elementary factorization 1-q^{rn}=(1-q^n)Σ_{j=0}^{r-1}q^{jn} then upgrades this to divisibility by [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Finally, because the denominator-clearing factor D_{d,n}(q) is coprime to [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2, one cancels D_{d,n}(q) from the cleared divisibility and recovers the exact theorem statement.

steps.derives: Let Δ_{d,r,n}(q) be the original theorem difference, let S_{d,r,n}(a,q) be the normalized auxiliary sum, let D_{d,n}(q)=∏_{k=0}^{n-1}(-q^d;q^d)_k, and let F_{d,r,n}(a,q)=D_{d,n}(q)(S_{d,r,n}(a,q)-[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}). Then F_{d,r,n}(1,q)=D_{d,n}(q)·Δ_{d,r,n}(q) in Z[q^{±1}].
steps.trivial_justification: For each summation index k, Lemma L1 rewrites the factor (q^d;q^d)_k^2/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k in the theorem summand as (q^d;q^d)_k/(-q^d;q^d)_k. Therefore the whole finite sum in Δ_{d,r,n}(q) becomes exactly S_{d,r,n}(1,q). Subtracting the same term [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2} from both expressions gives Δ_{d,r,n}(q)=S_{d,r,n}(1,q)-[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}. Multiplying by D_{d,n}(q) and using the definition of F_{d,r,n}(a,q) yields F_{d,r,n}(1,q)=D_{d,n}(q)·Δ_{d,r,n}(q).

steps.derives: The Laurent polynomial F_{d,r,n}(a,q) is divisible by [n]_q (a-q^{rn})(1-a q^{rn}) in Z[q^{±1},a^{±1}].
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the statement of Lemma L5 under the theorem hypotheses on d, r, and n.

steps.derives: The specialization F_{d,r,n}(1,q) is divisible by [n]_q (1-q^{rn})^2 in Z[q^{±1}].
steps.trivial_justification: Apply Lemma L3 to the Laurent polynomial H(a,q)=F_{d,r,n}(a,q) and to N=rn. Step A2 supplies the hypothesis that [n]_q(a-q^{rn})(1-a q^{rn}) divides H(a,q), so Lemma L3 gives the claimed divisibility of H(1,q)=F_{d,r,n}(1,q).

steps.derives: The specialization F_{d,r,n}(1,q) is divisible by [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 in Z[q^{±1}].
steps.trivial_justification: Step A3 gives a factorization F_{d,r,n}(1,q) = [n]_q (1-q^{rn})^2 H(q) for some H(q) in Z[q^{±1}]. Lemma L4 states that [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 divides [n]_q (1-q^{rn})^2 in Z[q], so there exists a polynomial B(q) with [n]_q (1-q^{rn})^2 = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 B(q). Substituting this into the factorization from A3 yields F_{d,r,n}(1,q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 (B(q)H(q)), which is exactly the desired divisibility.

steps.derives: Let M(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Then M(q) divides D_{d,n}(q)·Δ_{d,r,n}(q) in Z[q^{±1}].
steps.trivial_justification: Step A4 says that M(q) divides F_{d,r,n}(1,q). Step A1 identifies F_{d,r,n}(1,q) with D_{d,n}(q)·Δ_{d,r,n}(q). Replacing F_{d,r,n}(1,q) by this equal expression gives M(q) | D_{d,n}(q)·Δ_{d,r,n}(q).

Set M(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. By Step A5, M(q) divides D_{d,n}(q)·Δ_{d,r,n}(q) in Z[q^{±1}]. Lemma L2 gives gcd(D_{d,n}(q),M(q))=1 in Z[q]. Also M(0)=1 because [n]_q has constant term 1 and Φ_n(q) has constant term 1 for n>1. Therefore the hypotheses of Lemma L6 are satisfied with D=D_{d,n}(q), G=Δ_{d,r,n}(q), and M=M(q). Lemma L6 yields that M(q) divides Δ_{d,r,n}(q) in Z[q^{±1}]. By the definition of Δ_{d,r,n}(q), this divisibility is exactly the stated congruence of the original theorem.
